Week 09 · Hour 1 · explanation · 2 min

Which model would you deploy?

Model A has lower average error.

Is that enough if rare cases are costly?

Defined synthetic / analytic teaching example.
2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Which model would you deploy?. Illustrative absolute errors, not notebook measurements. Assume common response units and the same population. A is not automatically preferable: the deployment loss and tolerable tail error matter. Ask for missing group sizes and error costs; do not imply B is universally best. Visual purpose: Model A has lower average error. Is that enough if rare cases are costly? Week 09 · Hour 1 · explanation · 2 min

The evaluated population matters

Test risk averages over the test population.

Deployment risk averages over deployment.

Defined synthetic / analytic teaching example.
2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: The evaluated population matters. Define f as the fixed predictor and L as a specified loss. Finite test MAE estimates a population expectation under sampling assumptions; it is not the population expectation itself. Distribution changes can change the integral even with the same f. Visual purpose: Test risk averages over the test population. Deployment risk averages over deployment. Week 09 · Hour 1 · explanation · 2 min

Mixtures can hide a weak subgroup

Overall MAE is a count-weighted average.

Always retain subgroup sizes.

Defined synthetic / analytic teaching example.
2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Mixtures can hide a weak subgroup. Derive by partitioning the sum of absolute errors over disjoint exhaustive groups. The identity holds exactly for empirical MAE. It does not hold by averaging subgroup RMSE directly. Group definitions must not silently overlap. Visual purpose: Overall MAE is a count-weighted average. Always retain subgroup sizes. Counts constrain interpretation

Two errors are not two hundred errors.

Report empty groups as unavailable.

2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: Counts constrain interpretation. These are illustrative summaries. Same mean does not imply equal uncertainty. MAE preserves response units

MAE averages absolute residuals.

One large residual changes the metric

Predict the response as the fifth error grows.

Compare MAE with RMSE interactively.

Defined synthetic / analytic teaching example.
2 minutes / explanation. Teaching intent: One large residual changes the metric. The first four residuals are 0.1,-0.1,0.2,-0.2. A fifth residual t is appended, not substituted. Compare MAE with RMSE interactively. A pattern can reveal misspecification
